recipes.name: Pistachio Crusted Chicken
ingredients_raw: 2 large skinless, boneless chicken breast halves, cut into 1-inch strips

steps.text: Preheat the oven to 500 degrees F (260 degrees C). Lightly grease a baking sheet with cooking spray.
Combine pistachios and bread crumbs in a shallow bowl. Whisk Dijon mustard, olive oil, honey, salt, and pepper together in a separate bowl until smooth.
Dip chicken in Dijon mixture, then dredge in pistachio mixture until evenly coated. Place onto the prepared baking sheet.

Place in the preheated oven and turn the oven down to 375 degrees F (190 degrees C). Bake until chicken is no longer pink in the center and the juices run clear, about 20 minutes. An instant-read thermometer inserted into the center should read at least 165 degrees F (74 degrees C).

raw_recipe.headline: Pistachio Crusted Chicken
raw_recipe.description: Kids will love these quick pistachio chicken strips; adults will too! This recipe is very easy, and elegant. Anyone can make it, and everyone will enjoy it!

review.reviewBody: HELPFUL TIPS NOT MENTIONED: I've made this a part of our regular cycle for over a year now & feel lucky to have found it. Please do not substitute all cashews for this dish. I love cashews to death, but it doesn't nearly taste as good. In fact, I rated a cashew chicken recipe here worse b/c it doesn't compare. I use a full Planters Pistachio Lovers (6oz) can found next to the other peanuts at any grocery store and just remove the almonds (which makes a good snack while you make this quick dish..lol). I was skeptical about turning my oven to 500 & then moving the temp down, but it's amazing! Outside of that, I use italian breadcrumbs for all my recipes. Also, if you use the raspberry sauce from the "Pork Chops with Raspberry Sauce" recipe, be sure to add an additional T of raspberry to thicken it (on stove and simmer until half evaporated: 1/4C seedless raspberry jam, 2T orange juice, 2T white wine vinegar. Then take off stove & add a dab of butter to make silky).

This was so easy and delicious. I used pistachio meats from Trader Joe’s and pulsed them in the Magic Bullet to chop. I used gluten free bread crumbs and cut the mustard in half, which is just a personal preference. The toddlers and the grown ups loved it.

The family loved it!! Easy to prepare and came out the oven moist cooked on the inside and crisp on the outside. I used equal amounts of breadcrumbs and "crushed" pistachios : I put the crushed nuts in a plastic resealable bag and pummelled them for a couple of minutes using a meat tenderizer. Err on the side of making more of the Dijon mixture.

Great! Didn't have cashews so I used pecans...really tasty. Love that this doesn't call for egg! Chicken was SOOOOO tender, using the oils/honey mixture. One more change...was pressed for time sor I cooked on the skillet...4-5 mins each side...delish!!!

Best chicken my husband and father in law have ever had. I used a food processor to chop pistachios very small so they would stick. I also didn't cut into strips. Just used bone in skinless chicken thighs.

LOVED this!! Super yummy and easy to prepare. I followed the recipe almost exactly, except I didn't have enough pistachios so I also added some chopped up almonds. I made a dipping sauce out of what I had laying around: raspberry-jalapeno jelly, 2tsp balsamic vinegar, and 2tsp orange juice, nuked in the microwave for 2.5 minutes. Delish-- and gone in less than 10 minutes. Will definitely repeat.

Loved this recipe! Only thing I would suggest, is to bake on a rack to hemp prevent sogginess on the bottom. Will definitely be making again. We aren’t huge Dijon fans so I did 1 TBSP each of Mayo and yellow mustard. Turned out great.

Made these tonight and they turned out great! I too was nervous about having the oven high, then turning it down. I started off at 450 then went to 375. My tenders were done in about 15 minutes. I did add probably about 1/2 tsp of garlic powder to the honey mixture cause I add garlic to everything! Tasted great. Also I used italian bread crumbs, which next time I'll probaby use just a tad less of so it doesn't over power the nut so much. 

Overall, incredible and unique flavor! I'll definately be making this again and again!

This was an incredible meal. The only things I did different were to use Panco Bread Crumbs with Italian Seasoned bread crumbs. I did follow the directions of some of the other reviews and made a Raspberry dipping sauce. (1/4 cup of seedless raspberry jam, 2 tbps of each orange juice and white wine vinegar and reduced it to a medium thick sauce). I served mine with slightly steamed asparagus and vanilla glazed baby carrots.

This was delicious! The recipe did not specify raw or roasted pistachios; I used roasted and salted. I don't care for white meat chicken, so I used whole boneless, skinless chicken thighs (did not cut them up into strips) and baked them for 30 minutes, which was just right. The amount of sauce and 'breading' covered 8 thighs, then it ran out. 
As for the raspberry sauce: I added 1 tsp. cornstarch to about 1 oz. of water, shook it up in a small jar and stirred it into the sauce because it would not thicken. 
I used this as a dipping sauce on the side.

Tender and juicy but remember to bake at 375. One reviewer left it at 500, leaving it badly overdone. Note that I have stopped taken to grinding the pistachios to near-dust. They coat better and don't fall off.
I've been making this recipe for years now and its ALWAYS a hit! Super easy and full of flavor!
I had all ingredients on hand, but had to hand shuck the pistachio's. Kinda alot of work. Chicken was bland, nothing special for the work. Wouldn't make itagain

Made 9/22/25: VERY good. I followed reviewer Chef Joy’s recommend re: the Raspberry Sauce recipe and I think it works well here too. Me personally I think the sauce is a bit too sweet but my partner disagrees on that. Finding crushed pistachios was hard so I finally found a pre-shelled bag and ended up pounding them down using a mallet. Great way to work out any anger! 😂 If I had a food processor - that would have also worked (and probably better). The “crust” wasn’t as crispy as I would have like but again, I did find this very good. Served over farro and with a side of steamed broccoli. Thank you Julie!

My cousin sent this to me a few years ago and have been making ever since. I am not a fan of mixing savory and sweet so I eliminate the honey and use equal parts olive oil and djon. I use lightly salted pistachios. It really needs that little bit of saltiness. I eliminate the salt in the recipe because of the lightly salted pistachios.This chicken is on my regular dinner rotation.
Delish!! We loved this recipe!! We added a bit of stone ground mustard in place of half of the Dijon. Other than that, I followed the recipe exactly. Will make again.
Delicious recipe to change up the monotony of chicken breasts!
very tasty yall

Oh my goodness... This was fabulous. I followed the recommendations of others and served it with raspberry sauce from the pork recipe, and it was perfect. I've already made it twice for company, and will continue to do so in the future.
Easy to make and really juices and goos
